summary: Added the Phase 20 (Goal F7, ADR-024) coverage tests task 20.2 owns, without production changes. (1) The explicit direct-publisher absent-baseline test drives the internal ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync with a synthetic persisted Published state whose SourcePresence is Absent and no source artifact, and proves the removal boundary (RemoveImageAsync, media item update skipped) is the only mutation, the durable Restoration operation is written before it and committed, and SaveImageAsync/PersistItemUpdateAsync are never called. (2) The coordinator matrix gains the real-runtime NoFittingBadge case (native-guarded; a real SkiaBadgeRenderer through the coordinator on an owned session with a 10x10 retained baseline) proving the non-empty layout failure preserves the artwork with no mutation, and the 20.1 owned-restore case is strengthened with RemoveCalls==0 and the durable operation's Kind/Phase/Fence assertion. (3) Fence variants: restoration is permitted under Disable and Uninstall (coordinator and publisher, with the committed operation carrying the active fence) and refused without mutation under ItemRemoved (publisher's own second layer) and under an unreadable fence record (coordinator guard, fail-closed IsValid). (4) Crash recoverability: a Restoration ArtworkOperation created by the coordinator under the Normal fence is left non-terminal by an interrupted save, then resumed after a state-root restart by the ordinary recovery gate (ArtworkReconciler -> ArtworkRecoveryDecisions.Resume -> ResumeRestorationAsync) to Completed/Restored. (5) ArtworkGenerationResult.FromRestoration mapping is covered for Completed, Cancelled, NothingToReconcile, OwnershipLost, OwnershipUnknown, and RecoveryBlocked, including Preserved==false only for Restored and reason/operation/state propagation. (6) A coordinator constructed without the optional ArtworkLifecycleFenceStore drives the restore under Normal. acceptance_criteria.criterion: 1. acceptance_criteria.evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/ArtworkPublisherTests.cs: AbsentBaselineRestorationRemovesTheArrtagsImageWithoutSaveOrUpdate (synthetic Published state built by the new PublishedState(active, sourceBytes: null) helper through CaptureSession/CommitPublication). Asserts Completed + IsCommitted; RemoveCalls==1; SaveCalls==0 and UpdateCalls==0 with SavedBytes/SavedContentType null; host CurrentBytes null; the journal was at MutationStarted when RemoveImageAsync ran (PhaseAtRemove); the durable operation is Kind=Restoration, Phase=Committed, CandidateAfterPresence=Absent, CandidateAfterContentSha256/SourceArtifactId null, LifecycleFence=Normal, same OperationId as the result; state State=Restored, SourcePresence=Absent, ActiveImageIdentity/SourceArtifactId null. Sensitivity: probe A.

The non-owned empty-selection pass-through and the five other pass-through reasons with no mutation remain the 20.1 cases (not restated).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: 3. Fence variants: AllowsNewRestoration permits Normal/Disable/Uninstall and refuses ItemRemoved and an invalid fence record; restoration is permitted under Disable/Uninstall and refused (no mutation) under ItemRemoved and an invalid fence, covering both the coordinator guard and the publisher's own refusal second layer.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: 4. interpretations.question: How should the tests call the internal ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync when the test assembly has no InternalsVisibleTo access?
interpretations.chosen: A test-local reflection helper invokes the internal method directly; the production visibility boundary (internal, per ADR-024 clause 2 and its documentation) is left unchanged. No production code was modified.
interpretations.basis: The delegation requires the direct publisher absent-baseline test but also states production changes are allowed only if a test exposes a genuine defect; making the method public or adding InternalsVisibleTo would change the production assembly/API for test convenience. The test invokes the same method (same target instance and arguments) and asserts its observable effects.
interpretations.impact: Test-only mechanism. If the project later decides to grant test internals access, the helper can be replaced with a direct call without changing the assertions.

interpretations.question: How is 'restart' modeled in the crash-recoverability test when no process-kill hook exists?
interpretations.chosen: The save call is interrupted by an injected exception before any bytes are applied; the coordinator contains it and writes nothing after the durable operation/state, then the test constructs fresh StateRepository/stores/ArtworkPublisher/ArtworkReconciler instances over the same state root and reconciles. The asserted recoverability artifacts are the durable RestorePending state and the non-terminal Restoration operation.
interpretations.basis: A real restart reads exactly the durable records the test leaves; every post-crash write is skipped because the exception propagates out of ExecuteRestorationAsync into RestoreAsync's bounded catch, which persists nothing. The lifecycle tests already use the reconstructed-repository pattern (FenceSurvivesAReconstructedRepository).
interpretations.impact: The test proves the durable-record recoverability ADR-024 clause 3 requires; it is not a real process restart and is reported as such.

interpretations.question: Is the invalid-fence-record refusal proven at the publisher's own layer too?
interpretations.chosen: No: ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync receives an ArtworkLifecycleFence value, so an 'invalid record' can only be produced by the store read in the coordinator. The publisher's own second-layer refusal is covered with the ItemRemoved value it can receive; the invalid-record case is covered end-to-end through the coordinator guard (which refuses before calling the publisher) plus the direct refusal value at the publisher.
interpretations.basis: ArtworkLifecycleFenceState.Invalid reports IsValid=false with the most restrictive fence value (Uninstall) so a caller that only inspects the enum still fails closed; only the store-backed coordinator can observe Invalid. Probe D showed that if the coordinator's IsValid participation were dropped, the publisher would accept the reported Uninstall value and mutate.
interpretations.impact: None on shipped behavior; the coverage split is explicit in the tests.
